14233.title: Released binaries have High severity CVEs due to Go version 1.24.1
14233.feasibility_reason: The issue points out that released binaries contain CVEs because the Go toolchain/standard library version used in the build is outdated, and explicitly suggests upgrading the Go version in the Dockerfile and go.mod. Bumping the Go version is a straightforward and self-contained configuration/dependency update.
14233.problem_summary: Released Ollama binaries contain high and critical severity vulnerabilities in standard library packages (such as crypto/tls, os, net/url, and archive/zip) because they are built using an outdated Go compiler toolchain (Go 1.24.1).
14233.root_cause_hypothesis: The build configuration files, including go.mod, Dockerfile, build scripts, and GitHub Actions workflows, specify or pin an older Go version (Go 1.24.1) that contains unpatched Go standard library vulnerabilities.
14233.suggested_approach: Upgrade the Go toolchain version across the codebase (in go.mod, Dockerfiles, and CI workflows) to a patched Go release (e.g., Go 1.24.13, 1.25.7, or 1.26.0+), recompile the binary, and verify with govulncheck that standard library vulnerabilities are resolved.
implementation_steps: Update the go directive and toolchain directive in go.mod to the desired non-vulnerable Go version.
Update Dockerfile and related container build scripts to use the corresponding Go base image version.
Audit .github/workflows/ for actions/setup-go or hardcoded Go version strings and update them to match the new version.
Run go mod tidy and execute the full test suite to ensure compatibility with the updated Go version.
Build the Ollama binary and run govulncheck -mode=binary on the produced artifact to confirm all reported Go standard library CVEs are resolved.

15669.title: Both `qwen3.5:35b-a3b-coding-bf16` and `qwen3.6:35b-a3b-coding-bf16` are labeled as non-MLX, yet they are meant for macOS only
15669.feasibility_reason: The issue describes a simple metadata labeling bug where specific models are incorrectly marked or restricted, resulting in an incorrect error message on non-macOS platforms. This likely involves updating model definitions or registry entries in the backend configuration.
15669.problem_summary: Pulling standard non-MLX model variants (such as qwen3.5, qwen3.6, and gemma4 variants) on Linux or Windows fails with HTTP 412 'this model requires macOS'.
15669.root_cause_hypothesis: Model manifests hosted on the registry (or the server-side manifest validation logic) incorrectly assign macOS/Metal backend requirements to non-MLX GGUF model tags.
15669.suggested_approach: Audit and correct model manifest tags in the registry database/manifest repository to remove OS restrictions from standard GGUF variants, and verify pull validation logic in the Ollama client/server.
prerequisites: Access or repository control over Ollama model manifest definitions
Understanding of Ollama pull manifest architecture and OS restriction headers
implementation_steps: Audit registry model manifests for qwen3.5, qwen3.6, and gemma4 tags to locate invalid OS/architecture constraint metadata.
Update the manifest publishing pipeline and existing manifest tags to ensure non-MLX GGUF models do not declare macOS restrictions.
Review server pull validation logic (e.g. server/pull.go or registry handlers) to ensure client OS checks correctly parse model capabilities.
Verify pulling the updated model tags on Linux and Windows environments without encountering HTTP 412 errors.
